chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Adhere to the pomegranate, for it does not suffice a hungry person except that it satisfies him, nor does it satisfy a satiated person except that it increases his appetite.'

key_terms.أَمْرَأَهُ: Increased his appetite / made him desire more

ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of pomegranate according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the pomegranate's unique physiological balance, noting that it satisfies hunger for the hungry while stimulating appetite for the satiated. This dual nature reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of food as a means of maintaining both physical sustenance and spiritual vitality, aligning with the concept of *wasatiyyah* (moderation) in bodily needs. The narration underscores the prophetic tradition of utilizing natural remedies to regulate the body's state, ensuring neither deprivation nor excess.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the Pomegranate, for it would not be eaten by a hungry one except that it would suffice him, nor by a satiated one except that it would be order him (for more food)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘You must eat pomegranate; it suffices the hungry person and it is pleasant to satisfied ones’”
